title: Former Migori Governor Okoth Obado jailed for 25 years over 2018 murder of Sharon Otieno
key_points: The High Court in Nairobi on Friday sentenced former Migori Governor Okoth Obado to 25 years in prison.
His former aide Michael Oyamo also got 25 years, and former county official Caspal Obiero got 18 years.
The three were found guilty in July of killing university student Sharon Otieno in September 2018.
The judge said time already spent in custody will count, and made no order for compensation.
content:
Former Migori Governor Okoth Obado has been sentenced to 25 years in prison for the murder of university student Sharon Otieno in 2018. The sentence was given on Friday, November 27, at the High Court in Nairobi (Milimani), according to Citizen Digital and NTV.

The sentences

Justice Cecilia Githua sentenced three men:

  • Okoth Obado, former Governor of Migori County: 25 years.
  • Michael Juma Oyamo, his former personal assistant: 25 years.
  • Caspal Obiero, a former Migori County official: 18 years.

The Star reported that the time the three have already spent in custody will be counted as part of the sentence.

What happened in 2018

Sharon Otieno was a 26-year-old student at Rongo University. She was seven months pregnant when she was killed on September 3, 2018. Her body was found in a forest in Homa Bay County. She had been abducted together with a journalist, who escaped.

Citizen Digital and NTV reported that the court found the three men guilty of murder on July 23, 2026. NTV said the prosecution called 42 witnesses and presented 81 exhibits during the long trial.

What the judge said

The judge said she had looked at the points raised for the three men. These included that they had no earlier criminal record, their personal and health situations, and efforts to make peace with Sharon's family. But The Star reported she found that the seriousness of the crime outweighed these points.

Citizen Digital quoted the judge as saying Obado was "the architect of the criminal enterprise", meaning the person who planned it.

The court did not order the men to pay compensation to the family. According to The Star and Citizen Digital, the judge said there was not enough evidence of the family's losses to make such an order.

What the family asked for

Before the sentence, Sharon's parents told the court they wanted a non-custodial sentence for Obado, meaning he would not go to prison, so that he could keep supporting her children. NTV reported that her mother, Melinda Auma Rangili, said a death or life sentence would feel like another loss. The judge did not accept this request and chose prison.

The prosecution had argued for a strong sentence. NTV reported that state counsel Wangui Gichuhi told the court that murder is an offence against the State, not only against one family.

What happens next

The three men can appeal to the Court of Appeal under Kenyan law. None of the reports we read said whether they plan to do so, and their lawyers' reaction to the sentence was not reported.

The case has been followed closely across Kenya for eight years. It is one of the few cases in which a former governor has been convicted of murder.

Note: some reports spell Caspal Obiero's middle name differently (Ojwang or Ajwang), and describe his old job as county clerk or county employee.
